title: Cousin Henry in France, Germany during the war and the 1939 trip
summary: He names his cousin Henry Moreaux in France, recalls missing a train full of soldiers in Germany and a bus to Sweden.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: In France, you said your cousin was there. What is your cousin's name, the one in France?
Henry Moreaux. Where else did you go on that trip?

We went to Sweden, we went to Norway, Scotland -- oh, I forgot all the places. I know we passed through -- on the way to Sweden, we passed through Germany and we stopped at the railroad station, that was during the war -- getting on trains, soldiers and soldiers and getting off.
That was in 1933, or the next trip in '39?

I don't know which one it was. I guess it was -- yeah, because it was during the war, and that's why we missed the train. We were getting ready to go to Sweden and this train was just packed with soldiers, and they blow the whistle, just like you see in the movies, the foreign trains blow those whistles when they get ready to go. They blow the whistle, and we couldn't get on the train. The train left, you know?
So they had to hire a bus to take us to Sweden, across, you know.
Did you make the date on time?
What do you remember about that trip? That was the '39 trip, right?
Do you remember anything else about that trip?
Right now, I can't think of anything else; no, I can't remember nothing. I know we were terrific everywhere we went; everywhere in Europe.
